queries.text: Why is time to first token different from time between tokens?

lexical.query: Why is time to first token different from time between tokens?

results.title: Prefill and decode
results.text: Prompt prefill processes input tokens together. Autoregressive decode emits one new token per sequence per step. Time to first token and time between tokens describe different bottlenecks.

results.title: Temporal graph snapshots
results.text: Filter nodes and edges by evidence availability at the prediction cutoff. Exclude future events and reverse-edge leakage. Publication or ingestion time can differ from the event time recorded inside a document.

results.title: Continuous batching
results.text: Admit new sequences when existing sequences finish. Token scheduling improves accelerator utilization; admission limits prevent a long queue from exhausting memory.

results.title: Graph convolution
results.text: A GCN mixes self and neighbor features with symmetric degree normalization and a learned projection. Repeated propagation expands the receptive field and may blur distinctions between nodes.

results.title: KV cache budget
results.text: Attention keys and values are retained for previous tokens. Estimate bytes from layers, sequence length, key value heads, head dimension, concurrency and element precision.

results.title: Weight quantization
results.text: Low bit weight representations reduce parameter storage. Calibration, group size and quantization error affect quality. Weight precision alone does not determine KV cache precision or total device memory.

queries.text: How do document chunk boundaries affect retrieval context?

lexical.query: How do document chunk boundaries affect retrieval context?

results.title: Document chunking
results.text: Split documents with stable identifiers and useful boundaries. Retain headings and provenance. Very small chunks can lose context; very large chunks can dilute matching and exceed context budgets.

results.title: Lexical retrieval baseline
results.text: BM25 ranks documents using query term overlap, inverse document frequency and length normalization. It is a strong cheap baseline for exact names and terminology; no training judgments are needed.

results.title: Weight quantization
results.text: Low bit weight representations reduce parameter storage. Calibration, group size and quantization error affect quality. Weight precision alone does not determine KV cache precision or total device memory.

results.title: Candidate reranking
results.text: A second stage scores a bounded candidate set with a query and each document. Candidate recall bounds final ranking quality. Compare extra latency and quality against the first-stage baseline.
